In this paper, we accurately evaluate the excitation temperatures and their uncertainties from the absorption strengths of these components, and use them to determine the CMB temperature.

Along the line of sight toward the A component at $z=0.68466$, a rich molecular absorption system arising in the spiral galaxy has been detected, first discovered by (cite: WiklindCombes_1995).

They pointed out that, under optically thin conditions, the excitation temperatures of the rotational transitions of these molecules are expected to provide a reliable probe of $T_\mathrm{CMB}(z\!=\!0.68)$.
